 Sydney Sweeney has said she would have ‘more fun as James Bond
 Credit : Getty Images
 James Desborough
 Published 
 31 October 2026 4:00pm GMT
 Sydney Sweeney would make a wonderful Bond girl, a 007 actress has said.
 Trina Parks, 78, who played the assassin Thumper in 1971’s Diamonds Are Forever, said the next Bond needed a woman with “ownership over her sexuality”.
 Final screen tests for the next Bond are thought to have taken place this week, with the Crown’s Josh O’Connor , Jack Lowden, the Slow Horses actor, Callum Turner, the Eternity actor, and one unknown name vying for the role.
 Parks said: “Sydney would do a wonderful job. She has done quite a range of acting things and basically has got ownership of her sexual identity. Not only is she a talented actress, but has this Hollywood classic kind of style and poise, which really works for her projects and brand.
 “I feel for modern cinema and film-making and the future of Bond, audiences want to see a woman opposite Bond who is independent and has ownership of her sexuality. Sydney has those qualities.”
 Trina Parks played the assassin Thumper in 1971’s Diamonds Are Forever alongside Sean Connery as Bond
 Credit : Getty Images/Anwar Hussein
 She added: “The days of women just falling into bed with him have changed. To have the girl of the moment in Bond would be good. She definitely has a look that would fit into the Bond world
 “I don’t know much about her work, but she obviously can act because of the type of projects she has appeared in.”
 MGM Studio bosses, Nina Gold, the casting director, and Denis Villeneuve, the director, are secretly casting for actresses for the new Bond film.
 They have a shortlist of names on their radar, which is thought to include Sweeney, Margaret Qualley, Zendaya, Michelle Randolph, Nathalie Emmanuel and others. Sweeney and Zendaya previously worked together on HBO’s Euphoria.
 Sweeney has already been hired by Bond’s director for the upcoming adaptation of The Custom of the Country
 Parks said Zendaya would also make a strong candidate.
 “I enjoyed her in the Spider-Man movies,” she said. “Zendaya has this very strong screen prowess. And she would be another woman who would not be a pushover for Bond, which would be good thing.
 “I have always advocated for women of colour and greater representation in the movies and the Bond franchise has always been an advocate for them. The Broccolis were casting more people of colour many years before other Hollywood studios brought them in.”
 Zendaya, pictured at the Emmys last month, is reportedly also being considered for the role
 Credit : Randy Shropshire
 Jane Seymour, the Bond actress, 75, previously also backed Sweeney for the role.
 Asked whether Sweeney “would make a great Bond Girl?”, Seymour admitted: “Oh, I am sure she would.
 “I mean, she is gorgeous, talented. Why not?”
 Sweeney spoke about her interest in the Bond series last year after the franchise was bought by Amazon, saying: “I’ve always been a huge fan, and I’m excited and curious to see what they do with it.”
 Asked whether she would consider playing a Bond girl, she said she would have “ more fun as James Bond ”.
 Meanwhile, Gold has hired Sweeney to lead the cast of the upcoming feature film adaptation of Edith Wharton’s 1913 novel The Custom of the Country.
 One insider said Sweeney’s success in the past 18 months meant that hiring her would require MGM Studios to pay her at least £4.3m for the role of Bond girl.
 That fee would eclipse the earnings of Halle Berry, who took home around £3.1m for the role of Jinx alongside Pierce Brosnan in 2002’s Die Another Day.
 A New York producer, who has worked with the Bond franchise in the past, said: “Obviously casting James Bond is the priority to the public at the moment.
 “And sure that is well under way, but also there is a keen interest to make sure that the new Bond girl is something special and appealing to audiences aged in their teenage years to their 80s.
 “Sydney meets that standard – and then some. She is without a doubt the hottest female star in Hollywood at the moment.
 “She would relish appearing in an action role and would bring huge eyeballs to the Bond reboot.
 “Out of the female names being considered, her name is in the top tier.
 “The thing about Sydney is that she would command the biggest fee out of any Bond girl ever. Her fee is close to $6m and that would bring a whole heap of attention, sex appeal and excitement.”
